reviews.title: Stop trying to expand Meta AI.
reviews.body:
Meta's insistence on exploiting the work and data of its public creators, the backbone of the entire platform, is not only an egregious overstep of intellectual property but an incredibly malicious practice that impacts the privacy and data of all end users regardless of their presence on Meta platforms.

Even overlooking the blatant disregard towards its end users, the fact that Meta is going to such lengths to try and expand the assets it is allowed to scrape by masquerading blanket "consent" to pull from content that is not posted to its platforms only signifies that the venture into AI infrastructure has been largely unsuccessful. The only conceivable reason a company would need to pull from outside resources is because of a failure to produce results with what has already been harvested, so this decisions reflects extremely poorly on Meta's success as a business. Additionally, seeing as there are no safeguards for content that gets shared or reposted (and ultimately fed into Meta's AI without the creator's consent), Meta is largely leaving itself open to a myriad of lawsuits for the unlawful distribution, invasion, and usage of work created by users not on their platforms. Given that many large corporations and their employees also utilize Meta platforms, it would be unsurprising if additional issues arose over the scraping of their data and content without explicit knowledge or permission. Furthermore, allowing Meta AI to access chats from business accounts not only breaches privacy but will ultimately deter users from utilizing these features all together.

Meta's decision to pursue these avenues reflects very poorly on the corporation as a whole, but also on the integrity and security of your products. Continuing to pursue these decisions will only continue to alienate large portions of your end users, which will ultimately lead to a decrease in usage of Meta products all together. Reconsider.

reviews.title: Privacy Policy
reviews.body:
Meta Is Profiting From Creators’ Work Without Their Consent.

Beginning October 30, 2026, Instagram is reportedly expanding its use of business account content to train artificial intelligence, while denying U.S. creators the opt-out protections available in other countries.

My creativity is not Meta’s property. My work is not free training material. And my privacy is not theirs to exploit.

I have invested countless hours building my audience, creating original content, and earning the trust of my followers. Now Meta intends to extract even more value from that work without my meaningful consent, compensation, or control.

Meta gets the data. Meta trains the AI. Meta collects the profits.

What do creators get? Nothing. Not even a choice.

This is an exploitation of the very people whose creativity helped build Instagram into a multibillion-dollar platform.

Creators deserve transparency, meaningful consent, the right to opt out, and fair compensation when their work is used commercially.

Our content has value. Our consent matters. And Meta should not get to decide otherwise.

One star.
